column1: # The languages of each region in cloud/regions.tsv (one row per registry id;
# tests/test_region_languages.py checks that every registry row has one).
# languages = comma-separated ISO 639 codes (639-1 where there is one).
# The region's countries: those its site card names (web/generate.py
# REGIONS; "and dozens more" and "all of" mean every country of the
# continent), and for a region the border clip cuts to an outline, those of
# its row in cloud/region-outlines.tsv (Geofabrik's europe includes European
# Russia, so Russian is third in europe). For a region inside one country, the
# part of it the region covers. Its people: the people of those countries,
# or parts, inside the region. A neighbour that the box overlaps but the
# card does not name counts for nothing.
#  a. each country's official language, or, where it has several, the one
#     most of its people speak (de facto official counts: English in the
#     United States and the United Kingdom);
#  b. every other official language of those countries, or of a state,
#     province or constituent country the region covers (Wales, Catalonia,
#     Hawaii), that at least 1% of the region's people speak;
#  c. any other language that its people speak at home: at least two
#     million of them and at least 1%, or at least 10% of them;
#  d. French in Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia, which their signs and
#     administration use beside the official languages.
# A macrolanguage counts as one (zh: Mandarin, Cantonese, Wu; ar: the forms
# of Arabic), and Morocco's Tamazight varieties as zgh. c counts languages,
# not the varieties a country classes as dialects of its own language
# (Italy's Neapolitan, Sicilian, Venetian and Lombard; Bavarian and Swiss
# German in Germany and Switzerland). Iran's Luri is three languages (lrc,
# bqi, luz), each under two million speakers by Ethnologue's counts, so it
# is not listed; Gilaki and Mazandarani are just over.
# Order: most speakers first, first and second language together, among the
# region's people; near ties by the number of its countries where a language
# is official. Counts are rough (censuses, Ethnologue).
# records the row in map-config.json as regionLanguages. The viewer
# (resources/viewer, szRegionLanguages) reads only whether there is one: a
# map in another language than its base's then shows the visitor's name over
# the native one. It does not read the order; that is for later uses.
